## Description

`value_and_grad` currently calls `backward()` and reads each input's `.grad` buffer. Existing caller gradients therefore change the returned derivative, repeated calls accumulate unrelated gradients, and non-leaf inputs fail because their `.grad` is not populated. Outputs with multiple batch axes also fail because reducing only the last axis does not produce a scalar.

Compute the requested derivatives with `torch.autograd.grad` and an all-ones cotangent. This returns fresh gradients without accumulating into caller buffers, supports non-leaf points and arbitrary batch axes, and preserves the requested `argnums` order. Unused selected arguments receive their mathematically zero derivative. The current argument-selection API introduced in #1930 is retained.

The regressions check repeated evaluations with existing gradients, non-leaf points and unchanged ancestor gradients, scalar and tuple argument selections (including negative indices), unused arguments, and an empty selection.

## Validation

- All 16 new regression cases fail on unchanged upstream.
- [PyTorch validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geomstats/actions/runs/43829036128) passes the regressions and the complete existing `test_backend/test_autodiff.py` suite: 52 passed, 7 skipped.
- All changed executable lines are covered.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks pass.

## Description

`NFoldMetric.exp` and `log` determine the output batch shape before broadcasting their two inputs. For valid complementary batches such as `(2, 1)` and `(1, 3)`, the base metric computes all six results, but the final reshape still expects only one input's batch shape and raises an error. This also affects `Landmarks` and products whose points have multiple coordinate axes.

Derive the output batch shape from the already broadcasted inputs. The base metric evaluation stays vectorized, and singleton and unbatched axes keep their original meaning.

The regressions check analytic Euclidean, matrix, nested-product, landmark, and spherical results. They cover complementary batch axes in both orders, different batch ranks, one unbatched input, singleton batches, and unbatched controls. Scaled product metrics are included.

## Description

`RiemannianMetric.normal_basis` uses an Einstein summation that assumes every point is a matrix and that the basis has no batch axes. Consequently, normalizing an ordinary Euclidean or Poincare vector basis raises an error, as do batches of matrix bases and points with more than two coordinate axes.

Reshape each metric norm with one singleton axis per point-coordinate axis, then scale the corresponding tangent vector. This retains the existing matrix behavior, handles vector and tensor representations, and broadcasts base points using the metric's usual rules. The docstring now describes the supported basis and point shapes.

The regressions check analytic normalized bases in Euclidean, matrix, and nested-product spaces, local Poincare conformal factors, and affine-invariant SPD norms. They preserve batch and singleton axes and verify that inputs remain unchanged.

## Description

The higher-dimensional von Mises-Fisher sampler can return an empty array at valid high concentrations. For example, concentration `1e12` on the 3-sphere accepts no samples because subtracting nearly equal terms makes the rejection envelope zero. Larger finite concentrations can also overflow when computing its square. The log acceptance criterion and the transverse radius contain further cancellation-prone differences.

Evaluate the same Wood rejection law with stable algebraic expressions:

- Rationalize and scale the envelope so intermediate squares stay bounded.
- Compute the coordinate's difference from the reference node before multiplying by the concentration.
- Retain the complement of the axial coordinate to reconstruct the transverse radius without subtracting nearly equal squares.

The tests use a 450-digit Decimal evaluation of the original formulas as an independent reference for coordinates, radii, and acceptance decisions. They cover concentrations from zero through `1e200`, ordinary-concentration controls, genuine rejection draws, and rotated mean directions. The sampler API and distribution are unchanged.

## Validation

- On unchanged upstream, 19 regression cases fail and 6 controls pass on each backend.
- [NumPy, Autograd, and PyTorch validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geomstats/actions/runs/43833229777) passes the 25 regressions plus the existing von Mises-Fisher tests and spherical exponential round-trip controls: 41 passed, 8 deselected per backend.
- All changed executable lines are covered.

## Description

`value_and_grad` chooses the batch shape from a single input and constructs broadcast targets using the input's entire shape. This duplicates existing batch axes and can either raise an error or return a gradient summed over shared inputs. For example, pairwise Euclidean squared distances between shapes `(1, d)` and `(n, d)` should return `n` gradients for each argument, but the shared argument currently has the wrong gradient shape and values. Scalar points also lose their batch axes because slicing with `[:-0]` is empty.

Compute the common broadcast shape from every input's batch axes, then broadcast each input to that shape followed only by its point-coordinate axes before differentiating. The Autograd implementation uses broadcast views compatible with the project's minimum NumPy version.

The regressions check analytic gradients for scalar, vector, matrix, and mixed-rank points, including a real Euclidean distance call. This changes input broadcasting; the caller-state and backward-output issues are handled separately in #2239. The 15 PyTorch cases requiring multi-axis output differentiation are explicitly skipped here because they encounter that existing independent limitation.

## Validation

- Unchanged upstream: Autograd has 30 failures and 11 passing controls; PyTorch has 15 failures, 11 passing controls, and the 15 explicitly skipped multi-axis-output cases.
- [Isolated candidate validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geomstats/actions/runs/43835072035) passes the new regressions and existing autodiff suite: Autograd 77 passed / 7 skipped; PyTorch 62 passed / 22 skipped.

## Description

`ScipySolveIVP.integrate_t(..., t_eval=[0.0])` currently returns no state samples. SciPy produces empty evaluated arrays for a zero-length interval with this evaluation grid, and the wrapper propagates the empty result. Consequently, a numerical geodesic evaluated only at time zero does not return its base point.

For this single-initial-time request, let SciPy construct its native zero-interval result without an evaluation grid, then retain the initial sample exactly once. This preserves solver validation, status, dense-output metadata, and complex state conversion while restoring the requested output shape. Positive-length integrations continue through the existing path.

The regressions cover vector and matrix states, batched integrations, list/tuple/backend-array evaluation grids, RK45/Radau/BDF, complex dense output, and actual numerical Euclidean geodesics queried with scalar or array time zero. Positive-time integrations and SciPy's invalid-time rejection provide controls.

## Validation

- On unchanged upstream, 61 regression cases fail and 4 controls pass on every backend.
- [NumPy, Autograd, and PyTorch validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geomstats/actions/runs/43835072035) passes all 65 regressions plus the existing numerical exponential suite: 86 passed, 2 deselected per backend.
- All changed executable lines are covered.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks pass.

## Checklist

- [x] My pull request has a clear and explanatory title.
- [x] If necessary, my code is vectorized.
- [x] I added appropriate unit tests.
- [ ] I made sure the code passes all unit tests.
- [x] My PR follows PEP8 guidelines.
- [x] My PR follows geomstats coding style and API.
- [ ] My code is properly documented and I made sure the documentation renders properly.
- [x] I linked to issues and PRs that are relevant to this PR.

### Official CI follow-up

The later [Autograd job](https://github.com/geomstats/geomstats/actions/runs/43836389278/job/133193952209) fails `TestBetaMetric.test_inner_product_derivative_matrix_vec` when an Autograd `ArrayBox` reaches the in-place sparse assignment in `SymmetricMatrices.matrix_representation`, raising `ValueError: setting an array element with a sequence`. The [official job on unchanged base `2fc8e25`](https://github.com/geomstats/geomstats/actions/runs/42744796656/job/129594204622) contains the same exception and call chain. That reconstruction is unchanged here and is corrected separately in #2235. This identifies the existing exception path; the jobs did not record their original random parameters.

The [PyTorch job](https://github.com/geomstats/geomstats/actions/runs/43836389278/job/133193952059) fails `TestUnitNormedRowsPLTMatricesPullbackMetric.test_parallel_transport_ivp_transported_is_tangent` and `TestAACRegression.test_fit_and_predict_constant`. The original matrices and graph were not printed. Two deterministic replays therefore record complete inputs from the same fixture definitions, then compare exact base `2fc8e25` with this isolated patch using Python 3.13.18, PyTorch 2.15.0 CPU, NumPy 2.5.5, SciPy 1.18.1, and scikit-learn 1.9.1.

The [transport replay](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43871636636/job/133314061514) returns the same tangency result, `[True, True, True, False]`, on both versions. The transported vectors and endpoints also agree element-for-element, including matching NaNs. The [AAC replay](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43871636636/job/133314061031) returns the same total-space distances, `[0.784986936670632, 0.784986936670632]`, while both quotient-space distances are zero: the graph predictions differ only by vertex permutation.

Call tracing, verified first with an actual IVP positive control, shows that neither failing calculation invokes `numerics/ivp.py`. The replay artifacts retain the full input arrays and results. These comparisons establish existing failure modes and unchanged outputs; they do not claim to recover the original unrecorded random draws. An initial diagnostic run used the wrong callback argument order in its trace positive control; the linked follow-up corrects that diagnostic only, with no change to the candidate.
